title: Night Interruption and Light-Leak Risk
objective: Audit the true dark environment and manage night interruption according to intensity, spectrum, duration, timing, recurrence, and genotype.

terms.definition: Light exposure during the intended dark interval.
Unintended radiation entering or emitted within a dark production space.
Systematic measurement and inspection of the crop environment during the scheduled night.
Return toward vegetative growth after reproductive development under a changed signaling environment.

coreScience: Night interruption is a dose-and-timing problem, not a binary property of whether a person can see light. Biological effect depends on photon flux, wavelength, duration, position within the night, recurrence, cultivar sensitivity, canopy location, and prior induction.

Sources include door gaps, adjacent rooms, status LEDs, controller screens, dehumidifiers, cameras, emergency lighting, greenhouse twilight, work lights, timer overlap, and stuck spectral channels. Reflections can distribute a small source beyond the obvious line of sight.

Audit with an instrument suitable for very low light and the relevant spectrum; a standard high-range quantum sensor may lack the needed sensitivity. Inspect from crop positions after eyes adapt, test all equipment states, and record duration. Correct the source and verify the repair rather than relying on tape or assumptions.
cultivationRelevance: Repeated interruption can delay induction, create nonuniform transition, promote reversion-like growth, or confound sex-expression diagnosis in sensitive photoperiod genotypes.
Emergency and worker-safety systems must not be disabled casually. Lightproofing changes require code, egress, electrical, and operational review.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Date, dark-cycle time, instrument, detection capability, grid, equipment states, and operator.
Location, type, spectrum or color, direct/reflected path, measured intensity, duration, and recurrence.
Cultivar, stage, affected location, flowering timing, morphology, sex-expression observations, and photographs.
Shield, seal, control, schedule, or relocation action with safety approval.
Post-repair readings, complete equipment-state retest, monitoring frequency, and owner.

misconceptions: If I cannot see it, plants cannot: Human dark vision and plant photoreceptor sensitivity are different and spectrum-dependent.
Any single flash ruins the crop: Response depends on dose, timing, recurrence, genotype, and stage; investigate rather than assert.
Green work light is universally safe: Green sources can contain other wavelengths and sufficient photons to matter; safety requires measured validation.
evidenceLimits: Cannabis-specific dose-response thresholds for night interruption are poorly defined across genotypes. Use conservative dark control and site verification without inventing a universal allowable lux or PPFD.
